title: Dynamics for El Niño-La Niña asymmetry constrain equatorial-Pacific warming pattern
problem: Most climate models fail to accurately simulate the observed asymmetry between warm El Niño and cold La Niña phases, and the poorly understood dynamical causes for this deficiency create major uncertainty in future projections of tropical Pacific warming patterns.
method: The proposed method constrains climate model ensembles by their fidelity in simulating subsurface nonlinear dynamical heating, a key driver of ENSO asymmetry, to reduce uncertainty in projections of the future equatorial-Pacific warming pattern.
task: The task is to identify the dynamical causes of poor El Niño-La Niña asymmetry in climate models and demonstrate how correctly simulating these dynamics can reduce uncertainty and constrain projections of the future equatorial-Pacific warming pattern.

innovation: This paper demonstrates that subsurface nonlinear dynamical heating (NDH) is the key control on simulated El Niño-La Niña asymmetry, showing that models with realistic NDH reveal a linear relationship between future ENSO amplitude changes and the equatorial-Pacific warming pattern, thereby constraining future projections.
